title: User Experience
intro: User Experience covers how Constellation turns your data model and rules into screens: the four view types, form layouts, field configuration, dynamic behavior, portals and channels, and the styling and localization that finish the job. Expect scenario questions where two answers both seem to work and only one matches Pega's prescribed default or best practice.

objectives.objective: Views and templates; Full Page View customization (summary panel, promoted action, utilities)
summary: In Constellation, a view is a reusable arrangement of UI elements, and a form is the kind of view that collects input. Every view is rendered through a template, and the template handles layout, responsiveness, breakpoints, whitespace, wrapping and accessibility, so you pick a template and fill its regions instead of placing controls by hand. There are four view types: the Full Page View, Partial Views, List Views and Form Views. Pega creates form views for you, one per user step, and each one takes the step's name. Automation steps do not get a form view.

Pega adds the Full Page View automatically to every case type and data object, and each one has exactly one. It uses three panes: the summary panel on the left, tabs in the center, and the utilities pane on the right. You edit it on the UX tab, but the preview there only shows placeholders, so you need to run a case to see real data. The summary panel sits at the upper left at roughly mobile width, and when collapsed it switches to responsive mode. It holds the Details view, which shows the primary fields by default, and the Pulse view for posting and replying in the context of the case.

The promoted action is a single button in the case header. You never add a button component for it, because Pega picks it: the first stage-wide action other than Edit details, or if there is none, the first case-wide action. Only user actions can be promoted, never optional processes. The utilities pane holds widgets such as Attachments, Case operator, Tags, GenAI Coach, Followers, Prediction, Stakeholders and Related Cases, and it is hidden when no widgets are configured.
keyFacts: Four Constellation view types: Full Page View, Partial View, List View and Form View. Only Form Views can be editable; the other three are read-only.
Each case type or data object has exactly **one** Full Page View, which Pega adds automatically. You edit it on the UX tab.
Full Page View panes: summary (left), center tabs, and utilities (right). The UX tab preview shows placeholders, so run a case to see data.
The summary panel contains the Details view (primary fields by default) and the Pulse view.
Promoted action: the first stage-wide action other than Edit details, otherwise the first case-wide action. Only user actions qualify, and no button component is needed.
Default templates: Form view uses Default form, List view uses Table, and Partial view uses Details (One/Two/Three column, Sub tabs, Narrow-wide, Wide-narrow) or Dynamic tabs for lists.
List views can use table, timeline or gallery layouts, but data objects do not support timeline.
A form view created on the UX tab under Other Views cannot be linked to a step directly. Embed it in the step's top-level form instead.
Best practice: build views from the lowest embedded level upward, and embed views rather than individual fields, which avoids similarly named views being auto-generated in the data class.
Constellation view changes save automatically in real time. There is no save, cancel or revert.

rows: Main interface for a case or data object
One per case type/data object; 3 panes (summary, center tabs, utilities)
Reusable read-only fragment; defaults are Details and Preview
Confirmation view when enabled; Details and Dynamic tabs templates
Shows records from a data source
Table, timeline or gallery; default lists open cases with primary fields; no timeline for data objects
Collects input at a step; default Create and Edit views
Auto-created per user step (not automation steps); Default form template

examTraps: A second Full Page View or a separate full page for each stage is never right. There is exactly one per case type or data object.
Adding a button component to the header to make a promoted action is wrong, because the platform derives it. An optional **process** can never be the promoted action.
Blank data in the UX tab preview is not a defect. The preview only shows placeholders.
Partial, List and Full Page views are read-only. If a question needs data entry, the answer is a Form View.

objectives.objective: Default forms vs hierarchical forms (and multi-step forms)
summary: A form view normally uses the Default form template: one layout with one to three columns. Two columns is the recommended layout. Wide inputs such as Rich text, Text area, Radio group, Checkbox, Boolean and Attachment span both columns, and tab order runs left to right. Step instructions show on the form by default, and you can replace them with custom text or hide them.

A hierarchical form takes one form view and splits it into tabs called form groups. Use it when users can fill in the information in any order and you want less scrolling. Form groups are not independent or reusable views; they exist only inside that form. Do not use hierarchical forms inside a multi-step form, because tabs combined with Next and Previous buttons confuse users.

A multi-step form is still one assignment for one user, but it shows several views in sequence with Next and Previous, and Submit appears only on the last view. Navigation can be horizontal, vertical or standard. The default Create process is a multi-step form. The process option 'Allow users to go back to previous step' adds the Previous button.
keyFacts: Default form: a single layout with 1 to 3 columns. Two columns is the best practice.
Wide controls (Rich text, Text area, Radio group, Checkbox, Boolean, Attachment) span two columns, and tab order runs left to right.
Hierarchical form: one form view split into tabs (form groups) for information that can be completed in any order, which reduces scrolling.
Form groups are **not** independent or reusable views.
Do not put a hierarchical form inside a multi-step form.
Multi-step form: one assignment, one user, several views. Next and Previous move between views, and Submit appears only on the last view.
Multi-step navigation styles are horizontal, vertical and standard. The default Create process is a multi-step form.
Step instructions display by default and can be overridden with custom text or hidden.
Forms are views that collect input and carry action controls (submit, cancel, navigate). Not every view is a form.

rows: Most steps; a short to medium number of fields
2 columns recommended; wide inputs span 2 columns
One form view split into tabs (form groups)
Fields can be completed in any order; long forms with a lot of scrolling
Form groups are not reusable views; not inside multi-step forms
One assignment showing several views in sequence
One user enters data in a guided order (for example, Create)
Submit only on the last view; still a single assignment

examTraps: A multi-step form does **not** create several assignments and cannot route views to different users.
Making form groups reusable in other case types is not possible. Reuse needs real views, such as embedded views.
Choosing a hierarchical form for an ordered, guided entry is a mistake, because tabs allow any order. Choose a multi-step form when the order matters.

objectives.objective: Field settings, primary fields and field groups (model-driven controls)
summary: When you select a field in a view, its settings cover the field type, label settings, editing options, additional helper text, form messages (warnings) and field behavior such as Required. Required can be always on or conditional. Because the UI is model-driven, the field type decides the control. Pega pairs each field with the best control automatically, such as autocomplete, checkbox, dropdown, link, rich text editor or text input.

Primary fields are the key fields of a case type or data object. Pega adds them automatically to the Create, Edit, Details and List views, so they appear in the Details view of the summary panel and in default lists. In a case type data model, Label and Description are primary fields by default, and you can also set primary fields on data objects. A field group puts related fields under a header with optional instructions. It can be collapsed, shows a vertical line at runtime, and can display an embedded list.

Picking the right field type is a UX decision. Use Currency for money, not Decimal. Use Text (single line) for numeric identifiers that never take part in arithmetic, because Integer strips leading zeros. A Picklist can show as a drop-down or radio buttons when the list is short, or as a search box when there are many records or you need several properties. In Constellation, a cascading dropdown is two Picklist fields where the second is sourced from a data page that takes a parameter. Traditional UI used a section with On Change and an action set instead.
keyFacts: Field settings: field type, label, editing options, helper text, form messages (warnings), and behavior such as Required (always or conditional).
Primary fields are added automatically to the Create, Edit, Details and List views.
Label and Description are primary fields by default in a case type data model. Data objects can have primary fields too.
Field group: a header, optional instructions, collapsible, a vertical line at runtime, and it can display an embedded list.
Picklist display: Drop-down or Radio buttons for short lists, Search box for many records or when several properties are needed.
Constellation cascading dropdown: two Picklist fields plus a parameterized data page.
Use Currency (currency codes and separators) for money. Use Text (single line) for IDs and zip codes, because Integer strips leading zeros.
Embedded data lists show as a Table (editable or read-only) or a Field Group (for complex records). Case reference can show as Autocomplete, Dropdown or Table.
Data reference modes are Single, List and Many to Many. List displays are Table, Simple table, Combobox and Checkbox group.
Location shows a Google Map. Email and URL include built-in validation and render as action links.

rows: Drop-down (short list), Radio buttons (short list), Search box (many records or several properties)
Table (editable or read-only), Field Group (complex records)
Table, Simple table, Combobox, Checkbox group (modes: Single, List, Many to Many)
Read-only data from a parameterized data page outside the case

examTraps: Integer for an employee ID or zip code that keeps leading zeros is wrong. Use Text (single line).
Decimal for monetary amounts is wrong. Currency handles codes and separators.
A Constellation cascading dropdown does not use a section rule with an On Change action set. That is the Traditional UI approach.
Primary fields appear in views automatically. Adding them by hand to every Create and Details view is unnecessary.

objectives.objective: Patterns, conditional expressions and when rules for dynamic UI behavior (visible, disabled, required)
summary: Constellation UI is model-driven. The data model and rules produce the UI through patterns, which are reusable templates for forms, lists, dashboards and case management screens. When the rules change, the UI adapts automatically and stays responsive. This follows the separation-of-concerns principle and the center-out approach: logic sits at the center and channels present it. Because UI generation is centralized, accessibility (WCAG 2.1 and Section 508) is built in by default. A fix to a central component reaches every application without editing each screen.

Dynamic behavior is set per field with three properties. Visible defaults to Always and can be set to Custom condition, When rule, If not blank or If not zero. Disabled defaults to Never and can be Always, Custom condition or When rule. Required defaults to Never and can be Always, Custom condition or When rule. A custom condition is an expression for one-off logic, while a When rule suits complex or reusable logic. Dynamic UI responds in real time, reduces clutter and avoids full-page refreshes.
A When rule built in Dev Studio can be used by App Studio authors only after it is marked as a relevant record. When rules are one of the rule types that can be marked relevant.
keyFacts: Patterns are reusable UI templates (forms, lists, dashboards, case management screens) generated from the data model and rules.
The model-driven UI adapts automatically when rules change and is responsive by default.
Accessibility (WCAG 2.1, Section 508) is built in. Fix a central component once and every app inherits the fix.
Visible options: Always (default), Custom condition, When rule, If not blank, If not zero.
Disabled options: Never (default), Always, Custom condition, When rule.
Required options: Never (default), Always, Custom condition, When rule.
Custom condition: a one-off expression. When rule: complex or reusable logic.
Benefits: real-time response, less clutter, fewer full-page refreshes.
Dev Studio When rules must be marked as relevant records before they appear in App Studio pickers.

rows: Custom condition, When rule, If not blank, If not zero

examTraps: 'If not blank' and 'If not zero' exist only for **Visible**, not for Disabled or Required.
Defaults differ: Visible starts as Always, while Disabled and Required start as Never.
Building a When rule for logic used on a single field is overkill. A custom condition is intended for one-off logic, and a When rule for reuse or complexity.
A Dev Studio When rule that does not appear in App Studio is usually missing its relevant-record flag. It is not a bug in the When rule.

summary: A persona is the business representation of a type of user. A channel is the interface those users work through: web portals, mobile, messaging and voice. Conversational channels include Facebook Messenger, WhatsApp, Apple Messages for Business, SMS/MMS through Twilio, embedded chat, Amazon Alexa and Email, supported by Intelligent Virtual Assistants (IVA) and Email Bots. Personas can share channels, and persona and channel access can be configured per stage. On the Channels landing page, a lock icon means the required component has not been added from Marketplace.

Drafting personas and channels in the case lifecycle, for example assigning them to a release such as MLP1, is a planning step. It does **not** configure channel access. By default a persona can reach every page. To limit a portal to certain users, assign the persona when you configure that portal, for example a Manager Portal. Creating a persona also creates a default permission set, a work queue and an access group. Creating an access group does not create a persona.

A portal is the UI of an application, and it is built from landing pages. Constellation has two portal families. Standard work portals serve professionals doing complex, recurring work. Self-service portals provide a minimal, guided experience for occasional tasks done by customers or employees. The default portal is the Web Portal. You can run one portal with visibility based on persona or several portals. Portal templates are responsive and include a mobile-only layout.
keyFacts: Persona = who (a business user type). Channel = how they interact (web, mobile, messaging, voice).
The default persona is 'Users'. A new persona creates default permissions, a work queue and an access group.
Personas can share channels. Persona and channel access can be set per stage.
Drafting personas and channels in the lifecycle for a release does **not** restrict access. By default a persona can reach all pages.
To restrict a portal, assign the persona while configuring that portal.
A lock icon on the Channels landing page means the component has not been added (Marketplace).
'Add channel process' on a stage lists only channels that have already been added. It is used for channel-specific processes such as IVA.
Standard work portal: professional, complex and recurring work. Self-service portal: minimal, guided and occasional tasks.
The default portal is the Web Portal. Templates are responsive and include a mobile-only layout.
Every role has a default channel interface, such as Work Portal or a custom portal.

rows: Customers or employees doing occasional tasks
Landing pages (Home, My Work, Dashboard, Explore Data)

examTraps: Treating channels and personas as the same thing is a mistake. A persona is a user type, and a channel is an interface that several personas can share.
Assigning personas to channels in the lifecycle for a release is planning only. It is not access control.
A self-service portal is not the right choice for case workers who handle complex daily work.
Creating an access group does not create a persona. The reverse is true: a persona creates an access group.

objectives.objective: Landing page templates, themes, widgets and localization best practices
summary: The ready-made landing pages are Dashboard, Home, Explore Data, My Work and the Self-service Main page. Custom landing pages use the Default page, Tabbed page, Dashboard page or Inline Dashboard page template. A default landing page can use a column layout, with or without a banner, or a dynamic layout where you drag, drop and resize. A dashboard is a landing page of widgets showing summaries and KPIs for each persona, organized as template, then regions, then widgets. New dashboards are Private by default and can be Shared (with all users or with your access group) or Public. A copy keeps the visibility of its source. Portal widgets include Pulse, To do (my worklist, team members' worklists, or a work queue) and App announcement (a message plus a link button). A developer must add the Pulse widget to the portal navigation.

The available themes are Pegasus (the default), Aries, Self-Service and Bootes. To customize one, save it under a new name. The Themes landing page flags colors that fail WCAG contrast. Themes do not support inheritance, so to specialize a theme you save a copy into a higher ruleset. Keep the design system (themes, fonts, icons, templates) in the enterprise or COE layer. Design tokens store styling centrally for consistency across platforms and can be changed per component.

For localization, Pega uses the browser locale first, and the locale on the operator profile overrides it. If a locale ruleset is missing, users get English. A language pack must match both the platform version and the UI architecture. A translation package bundles the application's text as JSON or Excel, can be pre-translated with GenAI, and is imported on the Localization landing page under App Studio Settings. Constellation cannot localize decision tables or trees, case statuses, or radio buttons and dropdowns inside a table. Picklist values are left out of the package, so you add them by editing the localization file in Dev Studio. Dynamic values need the pyMessages rule. Radio buttons and dropdowns sourced from data pages need values entered on the Additional text tab. Test by changing the locale on the operator record in Dev Studio; you may need to log in again.
keyFacts: Ready-made landing pages: Dashboard, Home, Explore Data, My Work, Self-service Main page.
Custom landing page templates: Default page, Tabbed page, Dashboard page, Inline Dashboard page.
Dashboard visibility: Private (default for new dashboards), Shared (all users or your access group), Public. A copy keeps its source's visibility.
Portal widgets: Pulse, To do, App announcement. A developer must configure Pulse in the portal navigation.
Themes: Pegasus (default), Aries, Self-Service, Bootes. Customize with save-as. Themes have **no inheritance**, so save a copy into a higher ruleset.
The Themes landing page flags colors that fail WCAG contrast. Design tokens centralize styling.
Locale order: browser locale first, then the operator profile overrides it. A missing locale ruleset falls back to English.
A language pack must match the platform version **and** the UI architecture.
Constellation cannot localize decision tables or trees, case statuses, or radios and dropdowns inside a table.
Character encoding cannot be switched from UTF-8 to UTF-16 after installation.

rows: Picklist values missing from the translation package
Add them manually by editing the localization file in Dev Studio
Paragraph rules such as step instructions
Translate manually; edit the paragraph files (base and translated folders) in the package
Radio buttons or dropdowns sourced from a data page
Localization landing page, Additional text tab: enter values per row, rebuild and import
Decision tables or trees, case statuses, radios or dropdowns in a table

examTraps: Expecting a division theme to pick up enterprise theme changes through inheritance is wrong, because themes do not inherit.
A language pack that matches only the platform version is not enough. It must also match the UI architecture.
If the operator profile locale is set, it overrides the browser locale, not the other way around.
Dashboards are Private by default, not Public.

questions.stem: In the Vendor Onboarding case type, the Verification stage has two stage-only optional actions, in this order: the optional process 'Escalate review' and the user action 'Request documents'. Case-wide actions are Edit details, Change Stage and the user action 'Add note'. Which action is the promoted action while a case is in Verification?
options: Request documents
Escalate review
Change Stage
Add note
questions.explanation: The promoted action is the first stage-wide action other than Edit details, and only user actions can be promoted, so Request documents wins. Escalate review is listed first but is an optional process, which can never be promoted. Change Stage and Add note are case-wide actions, which are only used when no stage-wide user action qualifies.

questions.stem: A team is designing the Constellation views for a Supplier data object and a Contract case type. Which two statements about Constellation view types are correct? (Choose Two)
options: A Form View is the only view type that can contain editable fields
The Supplier data object has exactly one Full Page View, added automatically
A List View of Supplier records can use a timeline layout
A Partial View becomes editable when it is embedded in a step's form
questions.explanation: Form Views are the only editable view type, and each case type or data object gets exactly one Full Page View that Pega adds automatically. List Views support table, timeline and gallery layouts, but data objects do not support timeline. Partial Views are read-only wherever they are used, so embedding one in a form does not make its fields editable.

questions.stem: A business architect built a form view named 'Bank details' on the UX tab under Other Views. It must appear when users complete the 'Collect payment' step, which already has an auto-generated form view. What should the system architect do?
options: Embed Bank details in the Collect payment step's top-level form view
Select Bank details as the step's view in the step contextual pane
Add Bank details to the utilities pane of the Full Page View
Rebuild Bank details as a Partial View and attach it to the step
questions.explanation: A form view created from Other Views on the UX tab cannot be associated directly with a step, so it is embedded in the step's top-level form, which is the view Pega generated for the step. Selecting it directly in the step pane is the limitation itself. The utilities pane holds widgets such as Attachments and Tags, not step forms. A Partial View is read-only, so it could not collect bank details.

questions.stem: The Policy case type has a Policyholder field group, and Policyholder contains an embedded Dependents list. The team is about to build the case's views. Which two practices are recommended? (Choose Two)
options: Build the Dependent view first and work upward to the Policyholder view
Embed the Dependent view in the Policyholder view instead of adding its fields one by one
Add Dependent fields individually so Pega generates matching views in the data class
Save view changes manually before leaving, so they can be reverted if needed
questions.explanation: Best practice is to build views from the lowest embedded level upward and to embed views rather than individual fields. Adding fields one by one is exactly what causes Pega to auto-generate similarly named views in the data class, which is the clutter the practice avoids. Constellation view changes save automatically in real time, and there is no save, cancel or revert.

questions.stem: The 'Collect property details' step is a single assignment, not part of a multi-step form. It has 36 fields in three sections, Structure, Occupancy and Financials. Users fill the sections in whatever order suits them and complain about scrolling. Which design fits best?
options: Convert the form to a hierarchical form with a form group for each section
Turn the step into a multi-step form with one view per section
Keep the default form and increase it to three columns
Split the step into three assignments routed to the same user
questions.explanation: A hierarchical form splits one form view into tabs, which suits information that can be completed in any order and reduces scrolling. A multi-step form imposes an order through Next and Previous. Three columns is possible but goes against the two-column best practice, and the form is still one long layout. Three assignments add work items without solving the order or scrolling problem.

questions.stem: The Create stage of a Loan Application uses the default multi-step form with four views. Which two statements about this form are correct? (Choose Two)
options: All four views are completed by one user within a single assignment
The Submit button appears only on the last view
Each view can be routed to a different work queue
The navigation style must be horizontal because it is in the Create stage
questions.explanation: A multi-step form is one assignment for one user spread across several views. Next and Previous move between views, and Submit appears only on the last one. Because it is a single assignment, its views cannot be routed to different queues. Horizontal, vertical and standard navigation styles are all available, and nothing forces horizontal in the Create stage.

questions.stem: A form view uses the Default form template with two columns. It contains a Text area field among several Text (single line) fields. Which statement describes how this form lays out and navigates?
options: The Text area spans two columns, and tab order runs left to right
The Text area stays in one column, and tab order runs down each column
The Text area spans two columns, and tab order runs down each column
The Text area stays in one column, and tab order follows field creation order
questions.explanation: Wide inputs, including Text area, Rich text, Radio group, Checkbox, Boolean and Attachment, span two columns, and tab order on a default form runs left to right. The other options each get at least one of those two behaviors wrong, either keeping the wide field in one column or describing a column-by-column or creation-order tab sequence.

questions.stem: A Policy case needs 'Premium amount', charged in US dollars, and 'Postal code', with values such as 02134 that are never used in arithmetic. Which field types should be used?
options: Currency for Premium amount and Text (single line) for Postal code
Decimal for Premium amount and Integer for Postal code
Currency for Premium amount and Integer for Postal code
Decimal for Premium amount and Text (single line) for Postal code
questions.explanation: Currency handles currency codes and separators, so it is the right type for money. Integer strips leading zeros, so 02134 would display as 2134, and Text (single line) is the recommended type for codes and IDs that are not used in calculations. Every other option either uses Decimal for money or Integer for a value with leading zeros.

questions.stem: On a Constellation form, the 'Model' dropdown must list only the models for the 'Make' the user picked in the dropdown above it. Which configuration achieves this?
options: Two Picklist fields, with Model sourced from a data page parameterized by Make
A section with an On Change action set that refreshes the Model list
One Picklist field shown as a Search box that lists makes and models
Two Picklist fields, with Model shown as Radio buttons listing every model
questions.explanation: In Constellation a cascading dropdown uses two Picklist fields, and the second takes its values from a data page with a parameter, here the selected Make. A section with an On Change action set is the Traditional UI technique. A single Search box does not create a dependent second list. Radio buttons listing every model are meant for short lists and do not filter by Make.

questions.stem: A developer marks 'Account number' as a primary field in the Customer case type data model. No views have been edited. Where does Account number appear without further configuration?
options: In the Create, Edit, Details and List views
Only in the Details view of the summary panel
Only in List Views and Insights of the case type
In every Form View of every step in the lifecycle
questions.explanation: Primary fields are added automatically to the Create, Edit, Details and List views. The Details view in the summary panel does show primary fields by default, but it is not the only place. Insights are created from Explore Data queries, not from the primary field setting. Ordinary step Form Views do not receive primary fields automatically.

questions.stem: An Order case has 'Ordered items', a list where users enter a quantity and choose a product for each line and the data is stored in the case. It also has 'Ordering customer', chosen from existing customer records maintained outside the case. Which two field configurations fit? (Choose Two)
options: Ordered items as an Embedded data field, list of records
Ordering customer as a Data reference field, single record
Ordering customer as an Embedded data field, single record
Ordered items as a Query field sourced from a data page
questions.explanation: Embedded data stores user input inside the case, and a list of records suits the order lines. A Data reference reuses a data object from outside the case, which suits existing customer records, as one record. Embedded data for the customer is partly plausible because it is a single record, but it would copy user-entered data into the case instead of referencing the existing records. A Query field is read-only external data, so users could not enter quantities.

questions.stem: A senior system architect created the When rule 'HasCoApplicant' in Dev Studio in the loan case type's class. A business architect wants to use it for the Visible setting of six fields in App Studio, but it is not offered in the When rule list. What should be done?
options: Mark HasCoApplicant as a relevant record in Dev Studio
Rebuild the logic as a custom condition on each of the six fields
Set the six fields to Visible: If not blank on Has co-applicant
Move HasCoApplicant into the Pega Platform base ruleset
questions.explanation: Dev Studio rules such as When rules appear in App Studio pickers only when they are marked as relevant records. Custom conditions would work but are meant for one-off logic, and duplicating reused logic six times is poor practice. If not blank tests whether a value exists, which is not the same as the When rule's logic. Moving rules into the Pega base layer is never the approach, and you develop only in your own top layer.

questions.stem: A business architect is setting dynamic behavior on fields in a Constellation form view. Which two statements about the Visible, Disabled and Required settings are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Visible defaults to Always, while Required defaults to Never
If not zero is offered for Visible but not for Disabled
A custom condition is preferred over a When rule for logic reused across views
Disabled offers If not blank in addition to Custom condition and When rule
questions.explanation: Visible starts as Always, while Disabled and Required both start as Never. If not blank and If not zero exist only for Visible. Custom conditions are meant for one-off expressions, and a When rule is the choice for complex or reused logic. Disabled offers Never, Always, Custom condition and When rule, but not If not blank.

questions.stem: An accessibility audit finds a keyboard navigation defect in a Constellation table pattern used by twelve applications. The organization must meet WCAG 2.1. Which approach reflects how model-driven UI handles this?
options: Fix the central component once, and every application using it inherits the fix
Correct the table configuration in each view of each of the twelve applications
Enable an accessibility setting separately on each application's portal
Rebuild the affected screens as Traditional UI sections with custom markup
questions.explanation: Constellation generates screens from centralized patterns, so an accessibility fix made once in the central component propagates to every application, with no per-screen changes. Editing every view repeats work that the pattern approach exists to avoid. Accessibility is built in by default, not switched on per portal. Moving to Traditional UI sections would abandon the centralized patterns and add custom work.

questions.stem: In the lifecycle's Personas and Channels section, a team drafted the Manager persona with the Manager Portal for release MLP1. In testing, Manager users can still open every portal page. Only the Manager Portal should be available to them. What should the team do?
options: Assign the Manager persona when configuring the Manager Portal
Remove the Manager persona from the other stages of the lifecycle
Move the MLP1 release assignment to the current release
Lock the other portals on the Channels landing page
questions.explanation: Drafting personas and channels in the lifecycle is planning only and does not configure access, and by default a persona can reach all pages. To restrict a portal, assign the persona while configuring that portal. Changing stages or release labels changes the plan, not the access. A lock icon on the Channels landing page means a component has not been added from Marketplace. It is not an access control.

questions.stem: An insurer needs one portal for policyholders, who file a claim perhaps once a year with step-by-step help, and one for adjusters, who process complex claims every day. Which portal assignment is correct?
options: Self-service portal for policyholders, standard work portal for adjusters
Standard work portal for policyholders, self-service portal for adjusters
Self-service portal for both, because templates include a mobile-only layout
Standard work portal for both, with Private dashboards hiding adjuster work
questions.explanation: Self-service portals are minimal and guided for occasional workflows, which matches policyholders. Standard work portals suit professionals doing complex, recurring work, which matches adjusters. Swapping them reverses the purposes. Responsive templates with a mobile-only layout exist, but they do not make a self-service portal right for daily professional work. Dashboard visibility controls who sees a dashboard, not which portal type fits a user group.

questions.stem: A lead system architect is setting up user types and interfaces for a new Constellation application. Which two statements about personas, access groups and channels are correct? (Choose Two)
options: Creating a persona in App Studio automatically creates an access group
Several personas can share the same channel interface
Creating an access group in Dev Studio automatically creates a persona
Add channel process on a stage lists every channel available in Marketplace
questions.explanation: Creating a persona generates default permissions, a work queue and an access group, and personas can share channels. The reverse is not true: creating an access group does not create a persona. Add channel process lists only channels that have already been added to the application. Components still showing a lock icon are not offered.

questions.stem: A Constellation application imported a Spanish translation package. Spanish-locale users see translated labels and buttons, but case statuses and the results returned by a decision table still appear in English. What is the best explanation?
options: Constellation cannot localize case statuses or decision table and tree values
The operator profile locale is overriding the browser locale
The language pack matches the platform version but not the UI architecture
The translation package must be regenerated with GenAI pre-translation
questions.explanation: Constellation cannot localize decision tables and trees, case statuses, or radio buttons and dropdowns inside a table, so these values stay in the base language. A locale override would affect all text, not just these items. A language pack that does not match the UI architecture would cause broader problems than two element types. GenAI pre-translation helps produce translations but does not remove the platform limitation.

questions.stem: An enterprise Center of Excellence is building a corporate theme from Pegasus, and two divisions need small variations. Which two statements reflect correct practice? (Choose Two)
options: Customize by saving the theme under a new name rather than editing Pegasus
The Themes landing page flags colors that fail WCAG contrast
Division themes automatically inherit later changes to the enterprise theme
Design tokens must be redefined in each application that uses the theme
questions.explanation: Themes are customized by saving a copy under a new name, and the Themes landing page flags color combinations that fail WCAG contrast. Themes do not support inheritance, so a division copy saved into a higher ruleset does not pick up later enterprise changes. Design tokens exist to store styling centrally for consistency, not to be redefined in every application.

questions.stem: A team is localizing a Constellation application into French for the first time. Which two statements are correct? (Choose Two)
options: The language pack must match both the platform version and the UI architecture
Picklist values left out of the translation package are added by editing the localization file in Dev Studio
Dropdown values sourced from a data page are included automatically in the translation package
Character encoding can be switched from UTF-8 to UTF-16 after installation to support French
questions.explanation: A language pack must match the platform version and the UI architecture, and multi-value local properties such as picklists are omitted from the translation package, so you add them by editing the localization file in Dev Studio. Data-page-sourced radio buttons and dropdowns are not included automatically, because the data pages are empty when the package is generated, so you enter their values on the Additional text tab. Encoding cannot be switched from UTF-8 to UTF-16 after installation.
